name: Natural Resources Defense Council
mission: The Natural Resources Defense Council's (NRDC) purpose is to safeguard the Earth: its people, its plants and animals and the natural systems on which all life depends. We work to restore the integrity of the elements that sustain life - air, land, and water - and to defend endangered natural places. We seek to establish sustainability and good stewardship of the Earth as central ethical imperatives of human society. NRDC affirms the integral place of human beings in the environment. We strive to protect nature in ways that advance the long-term welfare of present and future generations. We work to foster the fundamental right of all people to have a voice in decisions that affect their environment.
theoryOfChange: The Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) outlines its approach to driving environmental change through a 'four-pronged approach: legal advocacy, science-based research, policy development, and public engagement.' This framework describes how NRDC uses these methods as 'replicable strategies for driving real environmental change' and is presented as an 'Environmental change framework infographic.' The organization emphasizes that its success is rooted in this clear approach, detailing how these core strategies are utilized to achieve impact.

Their governance is supported by a <cite id="13">large board of 33 members</cite>, providing diverse oversight for their complex legal and international operations. Furthermore, their <cite id="14">3-year revenue CAGR of 4.7%</cite> indicates steady growth and consistent donor support even in a competitive environmental landscape.
rich_narrative.summary: The Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) is a major environmental advocacy organization that works to <cite id="1">safeguard the earth, its people, and natural systems</cite>. founded in 1970, the organization has grown into a significant legal and policy force with <cite id="2">$193,144,386 in total revenue</cite> reported in FY2023. The organization operates with a <cite id="3">99/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, signaling a high level of institutional maturity and public accountability. Its work spans critical areas including <cite id="4">climate change, nature and wildlife, and human health</cite>. While the NRDC is an established leader in the environmental sector, its model focuses heavily on <cite id="5">legal action and policy advocacy</cite> rather than direct service delivery. This approach allows for systemic impact but results in a different evidence profile than charities providing tangible goods. Financially, the organization is stable, maintaining a <cite id="6">program expense ratio of 78.6%</cite> in FY2023. This meets the standard benchmark for efficiency, though it sits lower than some direct-aid peers. A notable characteristic of the NRDC is its <cite id="7">significant financial reserves</cite>, holding over two years of working capital. This provides immense stability but also suggests the organization has the capacity to deploy more funds toward its mission. For donors, the NRDC represents a balanced choice: a highly transparent institution with a <cite id="8">4.7% three-year revenue growth rate</cite> that tackles urgent global crises through a domestic-heavy operational lens.
